summary: @or-sdk/pgsql preinstall fetches Bun and executes obfuscated bundled payload
details: On `npm install`, package.json's preinstall runs `node setup.mjs`, which downloads a Bun runtime binary from `https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v<version>/<arch>.zip`, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it 0755, and then `execFileSync`s Bun against a bundled sibling file `math_init.js`. `math_init.js` is a 727KB Bun-compiled bundle (`// @bun @bun-cjs`) using string-array shuffle obfuscation (`WV8StW` shuffle helper over a multi-thousand-entry lookup array `n7gIxM`) and is not referenced by the package's declared PostgreSQL SDK code; its filename does not correspond to any advertised functionality. The preinstall dropper `setup.mjs` itself uses obfuscator-style mangled identifiers (`_0x488df8`, `_0x52943e`, functions named `mu`, `ra`, `dl`, `xn`, `xb`) with inline string-key lookup objects for constants like `"--version"`, `"/etc/os-release"`, `"bun"`, and the Bun release URL. Fetching an alternate runtime purely to execute a bundled, obfuscated, purpose-mismatched payload at install time is the alternate-runtime-dropper pattern: the alien runtime is used to hide execution from Node-based scanners while attacker-controlled bundled code runs on every install.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
